about: Editorial notes written from the research doc (as of 2026-10-21); every figure is the doc's, and project descriptions are general knowledge. Checked against the doc on 2026-10-25. Not advice.

HYPE.narrative: The doc's rank-1 sector is on-chain finance that earns real revenue, and Hyperliquid is its centre: its own L1 runs the largest perp DEX, and almost all fees go to buying back HYPE.
HYPE.standout: Per the doc: $1.4bn cumulative revenue, $1.26bn of buybacks, 57% of on-chain open interest, and TVL rising every month of the 2026 bear ($4.1bn to $7.4bn).
HYPE.thesis: Base case assumes the DeFi-2020 analogue holds: revenue keeps compounding while BTC recovers, so HYPE tracks BTC at its measured beta. Breaks if volume share keeps fragmenting (the doc notes 70% to 31%) or a bridge exploit hits.

ASTER.narrative: A newer perp DEX in the doc's rank-1 sector, launched while the market was fragmenting (Hyperliquid's volume share fell from 70% to 31%, per the doc).
ASTER.standout: Listed by the doc as a rank-1 candidate and among cycle 4's perp-DEX winners; the evidence is the sector's: perp DEXs at 12.3% of global futures and $633bn of 30-day volume.
ASTER.thesis: The projection treats ASTER as high-beta exposure to perp-DEX growth. It fails if incentive-driven volume fades once emissions slow, the usual fate of points-led launches.

LIT.narrative: Lighter is a zero-knowledge perp DEX in the rank-1 sector, aiming at retail with low or zero trading fees.
LIT.standout: Listed by the doc as a rank-1 candidate and among cycle 4's perp-DEX winners; the evidence is the sector's: perp DEXs at 12.3% of global futures and $633bn of 30-day volume.
LIT.thesis: Beta-scaled bet on perp DEXs continuing to take futures volume from exchanges. Risk: a zero-fee model leaves little revenue to accrue to the token.

JUP.narrative: Jupiter is Solana's main trade router and also runs perps, so it sits in the doc's on-chain-finance sector and benefits from Solana activity.
JUP.standout: Fee-earning venue on Solana, which the doc names (with Base) as cycle 4's retail-speculation chain; part of the revenue-to-token group the doc prefers.
JUP.thesis: Projection assumes Solana activity recovers with BTC. Breaks if Solana DEX volume stays depressed or token unlocks outpace buybacks.

AAVE.narrative: Aave is the largest lending protocol and a survivor from the 2020 DeFi cycle, the doc's model of a fundamentals sector that came through a bear intact.
AAVE.standout: The doc's cycle 3 table: AAVE ran about 200x (2020-21), and DeFi blue chips fell 80-90% in 2022 but survived and recovered. Its rule: every sector with real fee share survived the next bear.
AAVE.thesis: Treated as lower-beta DeFi blue chip. Upside depends on credit demand returning with prices; risk is rate competition from tokenized Treasuries.

PENDLE.narrative: Pendle splits yield-bearing tokens into principal and yield, the rail for trading on-chain yields; the doc lists it under fee-sharing DeFi and as a yield rail for RWA.
PENDLE.standout: Grew with stablecoin yields in cycle 4 (the doc: PENDLE about 7x low to peak); its volume rises with yield products like USDe.
PENDLE.thesis: Projection assumes on-chain yield markets grow with stablecoin supply. Breaks if rates fall and yield products shrink, the doc's named risk for the stablecoin sector.

ENA.narrative: Ethena issues USDe, a synthetic dollar backed by a hedged basis trade, the token play in the doc's stablecoin and payments sector.
ENA.standout: The doc: USDe went from zero to $14bn in cycle 4 and stablecoin supply is about $290-320bn and rising.
ENA.thesis: Base case assumes stablecoin supply keeps growing and funding rates stay positive. Breaks on yield compression (the doc's risk) or negative funding that shrinks USDe.

XPL.narrative: Plasma is a chain built for stablecoin payments, one of the doc's infrastructure plays on the 'boring rail' every sector settles on.
XPL.standout: Listed by the doc under stablecoin and payments infrastructure, which grows with usage rather than with BTC.
XPL.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled; the honest thesis is usage growth. Risk, per the doc: value accrues to private issuers like Tether and Circle rather than to chain tokens.

TRX.narrative: Tron carries a large share of USDT transfers, so it is the incumbent payments chain in the doc's stablecoin sector.
TRX.standout: Grows with stablecoin usage rather than speculation; the beta in the row above shows how closely it tracks BTC.
TRX.thesis: Low-beta projection. Risk: regulation of offshore stablecoin flows, and new payment chains taking share.

SKY.narrative: Sky is the rebrand of MakerDAO and issuer of USDS, the oldest decentralised stablecoin, in the doc's stablecoin sector.
SKY.standout: One of the DeFi survivors with real revenue, much of it from Treasury-backed collateral.
SKY.thesis: Assumes USDS supply and revenue grow. Breaks if falling rates cut collateral income, the doc's yield-compression risk.

ONDO.narrative: Ondo tokenizes Treasuries and stocks, the most direct token play on the doc's rank-3 RWA sector.
ONDO.standout: The doc: on-chain RWA ex-stablecoins went from $5bn (Jan 2025) to $38.6bn (Sep 2026); ONDO ran about 26x low to peak in cycle 4.
ONDO.thesis: Projection assumes the RWA grind continues: per the doc, RWA (with L1s) was positive in both 2024 and 2025 and had TradFi backers. Breaks if value stays captured off-chain or the token keeps trading at a large multiple of fees.

LINK.narrative: Chainlink supplies oracles and cross-chain messaging that tokenized assets depend on, so it spans the RWA sector and DeFi in general.
LINK.standout: In the doc's tables for two cycles: middleware in cycle 3 ($1.50 to $52) and RWA in cycle 4 ($5 to $30).
LINK.thesis: Lower-beta infrastructure bet on RWA growth. Risk: usage growth not translating into token demand.

SYRUP.narrative: Maple runs on-chain institutional lending (private credit), one of the doc's RWA sub-sectors.
SYRUP.standout: The doc: tokenized private credit $7.9bn by Sep 2026.
SYRUP.thesis: Projection scales with BTC; the thesis is credit growth. Breaks on borrower defaults, the risk that ended Maple's first version in 2022.

PLUME.narrative: Plume is a chain built for real-world assets, listed by the doc in the RWA sector.
PLUME.standout: Rides the doc's RWA growth figures, but as a newer token it carries unlock risk.
PLUME.thesis: High-beta RWA exposure. Risk, per the doc: 56% of tokenized assets show zero weekly activity, so assets on a chain need not mean usage.

CFG.narrative: Centrifuge pioneered on-chain credit from real-world receivables, part of the doc's RWA sector.
CFG.standout: Long-running RWA infrastructure with institutional partners.
CFG.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled. Risk: smaller, older token losing share to better-funded RWA platforms.

TAO.narrative: Bittensor runs subnets that pay for AI work, the infrastructure side of the doc's rank-5 'second AI wave'.
TAO.standout: The doc points to subnet revenue as the usage metric that survived the first AI-agent blow-off.
TAO.thesis: Assumes the 2017-to-2020 pattern: a sector that blew off returns with fundamentals. Breaks if AI compute never needs a token, the doc's main risk.

VIRTUAL.narrative: Virtuals is the AI-agent launchpad of cycle 4, now pushing agent payments (ACP, x402), the doc's second-wave AI play.
VIRTUAL.standout: The doc: revenue peaked at $1.02m a day in Jan 2025 then fell 96%, while x402 processed $600m by Nov 2025.
VIRTUAL.thesis: Projection assumes agent payments become real usage. Breaks if agent tokens stay wrappers, the doc's risk, as first-wave tokens did.

RENDER.narrative: Render sells decentralised GPU rendering and compute, the decentralised-compute half of the doc's AI x crypto sector.
RENDER.standout: One of the cycle-4 AI infrastructure names that kept real paying work.
RENDER.thesis: Beta-scaled AI-compute exposure. Risk: centralised clouds remain cheaper and simpler for AI workloads.

AKT.narrative: Akash is a decentralised cloud marketplace, in the doc's decentralised-compute group.
AKT.standout: Usage-based revenue from compute leases rather than speculation.
AKT.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled. Risk: small market share against hyperscalers.

GRASS.narrative: Grass pays users for spare bandwidth used to gather AI training data, an AI x DePIN play the doc flags as a top 2026 narrative.
GRASS.standout: The doc cites CoinGecko naming AI x DePIN a leading 2026 narrative.
GRASS.thesis: High-beta bet on AI data demand. Risk: legal and data-sourcing limits, and emissions-driven supply.

IO.narrative: io.net aggregates GPUs for AI workloads, in the doc's decentralised-compute group.
IO.standout: Part of the AI compute cohort the doc expects to return on usage.
IO.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled. Risk: utilisation, and unlocks from a recent launch.

SOL.narrative: Solana is the doc's rank-6 high-throughput L1 and the chain that hosted the 2024 retail cycle; L1s led every mid-cycle recovery.
SOL.standout: The doc: L1 narrative +80% in 2025, one of three positive; Solana ETF live; SOL ran about 37x low to peak in cycle 4.
SOL.thesis: Projection is the cleanest beta-to-BTC case in the list. Breaks if retail issuance moves to another chain: the doc says the memecoin primitive returns each cycle, but on a new launchpad or chain.

SUI.narrative: Sui is a newer high-throughput L1, in the doc's rank-6 group.
SUI.standout: The doc: SUI ran about 13x low to peak in cycle 4.
SUI.thesis: High-beta L1 exposure. Risk, per the doc: new-launch L1 tokens carry low-float, high-valuation unlock risk.

TON.narrative: TON is Telegram's chain; the doc names it the consumer on-ramp via Telegram mini-apps and a place to watch for the next memecoin launchpad.
TON.standout: Distribution through Telegram's user base rather than DeFi metrics.
TON.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled. Risk: Telegram-specific regulatory events and weak on-chain activity outside mini-apps.

ZEC.narrative: Zcash is the doc's rank-7 privacy sleeve: privacy coins rally when BTC consolidates.
ZEC.standout: The doc: ZEC ran 20x+ in Q4 2025, after BTC's top; privacy and quantum-resistant sectors led H1 2025 sector gains.
ZEC.thesis: Speculative sleeve; the projection is mechanical. Breaks on exchange delistings, the doc's main risk.

XMR.narrative: Monero is the other privacy coin in the doc's sleeve, mirroring Darkcoin 2014 and Monero 2017.
XMR.standout: Longest-lived privacy coin; trades on fewer venues after delistings.
XMR.thesis: Lower-beta privacy exposure. Risk: further delistings and regulatory pressure.

CORE.narrative: Core is an EVM chain secured by bitcoin staking, the doc's rank-8 BTC-fi idea of making the largest asset productive.
CORE.standout: The doc: ETF-era holders want yield on BTC.
CORE.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled. The doc's own caveat: 2024's BTC-layer tokens all failed to hold, and value tends to accrue to BTC, not the layer.

STX.narrative: Stacks is the longest-running Bitcoin layer with sBTC, in the doc's BTC-fi group.
STX.standout: The doc names STX among the 2024 BTC-L2 tokens that failed to hold.
STX.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled. Risk: low usage so far, per the doc.

DASH.narrative: Dash (formerly Darkcoin) is the oldest coin in the doc's privacy sleeve: it led Anonymity v1 in 2014 and the privacy-coin run of 2017.
DASH.standout: The doc: Darkcoin $0.3 to $15 (May 2014, ~50x) and DASH $10 to $1,550 (Jan 2018, ~150x); listed again among cycle 4's privacy names.
DASH.thesis: Speculative sleeve; the projection is mechanical. Breaks on exchange delistings, the doc's main risk for privacy.

BABY.narrative: Babylon lets bitcoin be staked to secure other chains, the doc's rank-8 BTC-fi idea of making the largest asset productive.
BABY.standout: Named by the doc as a rank-8 play; the doc's case is that ETF-era holders want yield on BTC.
BABY.thesis: Projection is beta-scaled. The doc's caveat: 2024's BTC-layer tokens all failed to hold, and value tends to accrue to BTC, not the layer.

NEAR.narrative: NEAR is a sharded proof-of-stake L1 that markets itself as the chain for AI agents; classifiers file it as an L1 first and AI second, so it sits with the doc's rank-6 high-throughput L1s.
NEAR.standout: Not in the research doc's candidate table (added on request); the doc's case for the sector is its own: L1 narrative +80% in 2025, and L1s led every mid-cycle recovery.
NEAR.thesis: Projection is BTC beta with NEAR's own fees, TVL and unlocks; no doc figures. Breaks if the AI-chain positioning does not turn into fees, or activity stays on the larger L1s.
